claim: The Semrock BrightLine FF01-432/36-32 bandpass filter is specified with a centre wavelength of 432 nm and a full width at half maximum of 36 nm, giving a nominal passband of 414.0 to 450.0 nm.

numbers.name: filter_centre_wavelength
numbers.note: the designated centre. A nominal specification at the precision it was specified to -- 5.3 forbids dressing a nominal designation in a precision back-computed from a calibration, which is the 20.078x case, and does not forbid this. Same treatment objective_mrd70040 gives its NA.

validity_conditions: A VENDOR SPECIFICATION ABOUT A PART, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT E5. This does not come through the prior repository even though that is where the part number was found: the passband is Semrock's published specification of FF01-432/36-32, and a part number is a type. Whether this part is in this laboratory's wheel is a SEPARATE claim at E5 (emission_wheel_filter_positions); whether it is in position 3 is another (emission_wheel_red_arm_is_position_3). Keeping them apart is what lets the band arrive at E3 the moment somebody confirms the part off the engraving, instead of the whole chain being dragged to E5. NOMINAL PASSBAND, NOT A MEASURED CURVE. 414.0-450.0 nm is centre plus or minus half the FWHM. A real filter's edges are steeper than that and its blocking is wavelength dependent, so this is a triage figure: adequate for deciding which band collects a dye, not for a blocking calculation. The vendor publishes measured curves and none has been obtained. `validity` pins the passband so a query at another wavelength returns `disjoint` rather than a value. THE SOURCE TOKEN IS SLUGGED AND THE PART NUMBER IS NOT. `source` reads `spec:FF01-432-36-32` because common.schema.json's source pattern allows [A-Za-z0-9_.:@-] and a solidus is not in it -- while every bandpass part number in optics is written centre/width, so the pattern excludes the canonical form of an entire class of part. The true part number `FF01-432/36-32` is in `identifiers.part_number`, which is where an exact designation belongs anyway, and the slug is reversible. Raised with manager-librarian rather than left as a silent mangling: a source token that does not match the part it names is the kind of thing that reads fine until somebody greps for it.
